description: Exercises the ROTATION in-force rule against a real two-binding chain (#133): kya-l4-genesis (SLH-DSA key 638c79a2…, anchored on Ethereum mainnet at 1785423299) rotated to kya-l4-rotation-1 (NEW SLH-DSA key 8488157a…, links predecessor via predecessor_content_address). The rotation binding is genuine, not fabricated: it is dual-signed over its own content-address by the PREDECESSOR key (continuity) and the new key (possession) — see pq-key-binding-v0.rotation.json, verified in the deep lane. Run with cutoff_enforce.py: `python3 cutoff_enforce.py pq-key-binding-v0.rotation-vectors.json`. Each case asserts the RESOLUTION step (which binding governs at the artifact's anchor time, by which reason) — the boundary between two rotations is the point, not the aggregate. Cases 6-7 close the loop: after a rotation, a POST-CUTOFF artifact must carry a companion under the NEW in-force key; a companion valid only under the retired key no longer admits — that is rotation actually being enforced. rotation-1's binding_anchor_time (1788000000) is its intended on-chain anchor; the mainnet record() for it is the production-hardening step (as vector 2 was for genesis).

cases.name: exactly AT rotation anchor → rotation-1 governs
post-cutoff after rotation, companion under NEW in-force key → admit
post-cutoff after rotation, companion under RETIRED key → reject (rotation enforced)
